youtube_title: Westville, Indiana: the morning Lincoln's funeral train came through (Westville request)
youtube:
You asked for Westville! On May 1, 1865, Abraham Lincoln's funeral train rolled north from Indianapolis through the night, past mourners standing by bonfires and torches. Shortly before 8 in the morning, it reached Westville; the town's 1965 marker says it stopped briefly there. Lincoln's son Willie, who died in 1862, made the trip with him. Up the line in Michigan City, the train stopped beneath an arch of roses and evergreens, and later that morning Lincoln left Indiana, where he grew up, for the last time. One famous Chicago Tribune description of the day (2,000 mourners and a choir singing "The Departed") is placed in Westville by some histories and in Michigan City by others, so we left it out. If your family has the story, tell us! Comment your town, and it could be next! #Westville #LaPorteCounty #AbrahamLincoln #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Westville Women's Club marker (1965), via the Historical Marker Database; Fern Eddy Schultz, LaPorte County Historian, What's New LaPorte (2009); The Times of Northwest Indiana (2015); Indiana Historical Bureau (Lincoln Funeral Train marker, Michigan City; Lincoln Funeral Train, parts two and three); TIME; American Battlefield Trust; National Park Service; Monon Railroad Historical-Technical Society. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
